A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Step Guided Reasoning (SGR) work. Their main text, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching the retained prompts and example across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original SGR experiments using Qwen2-72B-Instruct on MATH, AMC23, and AIME24, together with step-count and step-length analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments across multiple models and benchmarks, including component ablations and token-use analyses in Section 3.

M1.justification: Section 2.1 changes the stated minimum step-length unit from tokens to characters, revising the inference stopping rule. The guidance/answer loop and Appendix A.1 prompts remain unchanged. v2 also documents duplicate-step deletion and resampling, without establishing when that implementation detail was introduced.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluations on MMLU-STEM and the English, text-only mathematics-competition subset of OlympiadBench, substantially broadening the evaluated domains and problem populations. It explicitly reports MATH levels 1–5; v1 mainly reports sampled level-5 problems, although a footnote briefly claims consistent full-MATH results.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's CoT and reference-model comparisons, v2 evaluates five-shot Step-Back Prompting and BoN@16/@32. Table 1 adds QwQ-32B-Preview and additional Qwen-Math models and replaces GPT-4 with GPT-4o. Table 3 adds comparisons with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B.

E3.justification: The main reported MATH evaluation changes from 100 sampled level-5 problems to all 5,000 test problems. v2 adds three SGR base-model configurations, replaces manual AMC23/AIME24 grading with the stated GPT-4 validation procedure, and pools results across top_p values 0.7 and 1.0 instead of displaying them separately. New baseline experiments introduce five-shot prompting and 16/32-candidate selection protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds Stage-I-only and Stage-II-only ablations in Section 3.4/Table 2 and token-count versus accuracy comparisons in Figure 4. The existing step-count and step-length analyses are revised to examine Qwen2-7B across MATH difficulty levels. The train-station case study is retained, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly states that experiments run three times and report average accuracy. v2 omits that repeated-run count and instead describes averaging across two top_p settings. This changes statistical reporting without establishing that fewer runs occurred. Neither version reports confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical evidence is substantially replaced and expanded. For example, Qwen2-72B SGR scores 67% on v1's sampled MATH level-5 evaluation at top_p 0.7, versus 65.6% under v2's full-test, pooled reporting; these different settings do not establish a performance decline. v2 also adds STEM/OLY results, component-ablation outcomes, distilled-model comparisons, and token-cost findings.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. v2's iteration notation and expanded discussion of reasoning steps describe the operational method without introducing substantive formal theory.

C1.justification: v2 broadens the headline claims from mathematical improvements demonstrated principally with Qwen2-72B to stability and generalization across model sizes, families, and STEM tasks. It explicitly emphasizes avoiding reward models. The abstract adds the claim that Qwen2-72B with SGR exceeds Qwen2.5-Math-72B on MMLU-STEM, reporting 90.9% versus 87.3%.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation of Stage I failing on OlympiadBench through question repetition and interprets why Stage II alone can perform better. It also discusses instruction-following limitations of mathematics-specialized models. The limitations section replaces the sampled-MATH and grading concerns with memory/precision constraints and uncertainty about applicability to more challenging AIGC tasks.

D1.justification: v2 adds numeric-precision disclosures, duplicate-step resampling instructions, dataset counts and selection tags in Appendix A.2, and baseline implementation details. v1's 2–10-minute inference estimate is replaced by a reported mean of 6,384 MATH output tokens for Qwen2-7B. These refine implementation documentation while retaining the same four SGR prompt templates.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially expands positioning around Best-of-N, Tree-of-Thought, reward-guided search, and test-time computation. QwQ and DeepSeek-R1 introduce comparisons with slow-thinking and distilled models. Section 2.2 also explicitly attributes the initial guidance stage to Step-Back Prompting. These changes exceed bibliographic updates to already cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method exposition undergo extensive rewriting, including Stage I/II terminology and expanded explanations of guidance and step answers. Experimental setup is reorganized, a separate ablation subsection and dataset appendix are introduced, and the authorship line expands.

P2.justification: The compact original results table becomes an extensive grouped mathematics/STEM display with color coding, supplemented by two new tables. Figure 1 is redrawn, the step-analysis plots are redesigned, and a token-cost scatter plot is added. The existing train comparison moves from main-text Figure 3 to Appendix A.4/Figure 5.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's limited main evaluation through full-test MATH reporting, multiple model families, SBP/BoN controls, component ablations, and token-cost analysis. These make generality, component usefulness, and computational tradeoffs much more assessable. Reporting weaknesses remain: the three-run statement disappears, and Table 3 prints incorrect +12.3 improvements for both distilled models. These defects reduce precision but do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support.
